title: Term Life Insurance Beneficiary Designations
content:
**Term Life Insurance — beneficiary designation rules.** The owner names primary and contingent beneficiaries; the insured, if not the owner, has no say.

| Rule | Content |
|---|---|
| Status | A beneficiary designation is recorded only while the policy status on record is applied, in force or grace period |
| Changed designation | Recorded only from a beneficiary change request signed by the owner, and, where the current designation names an irrevocable beneficiary, also signed in consent by that beneficiary |
| Effect | A new designation replaces the whole earlier designation and takes effect on the date the owner signed it, provided the owner signed it while the insured was living; Ashgrove is discharged for any payment made before the request was received |
| Shares | Whole percents of at least the product's smallest share; the shares within each class must total 100 |
| Number | No more than the product's maximum number of primary beneficiaries |
| Who may be named | A trust or the estate may be named; a minor may be named, but the minor's share is paid under the death claim provisions |
| After death | No change is accepted after the insured's death |

### Hypothetical checks

- Primaries at 50%, 30% and 20% total 100 — acceptable; 50%, 30% and 15% total 95 — not acceptable.
- A share of 33.5% is not a whole percent — not acceptable.
- A change request signed by the owner where the current designation names an irrevocable beneficiary who has not signed in consent — not recorded.
- A designation signed on 3 May by an owner, the insured dying on 5 May and the request reaching Ashgrove on 9 May — the designation took effect on 3 May; any payment made before 9 May discharges Ashgrove.
